open_points.subject: A17 path traversal base
open_points.text: “a relative path starts at the kernel's working directory” states the base only for relative paths while empty components, including the leading component of an absolute path, are skipped
open_points.question: From which opened directory descriptor does component-by-component traversal of an absolute configuration or credential path begin?
options: the kernel's working directory after merely recognizing that the path was absolute

open_points.subject: A18 SQLite database location
open_points.text: “Every file the store opens itself is opened relative to the data directory it holds open from the start” but “The database file and its journal are opened by SQLite”
open_points.question: How must SQLite be made to open the database and auxiliary files relative to the held-open data-directory descriptor, so replacement or renaming of the configured pathname cannot redirect it?
options: open through a Linux descriptor path such as /proc/self/fd/<fd>
let SQLite resolve the configured data-directory pathname again
treat the held descriptor guarantee as not applying to SQLite files
open_points.default_guess: open SQLite through the held directory descriptor using a Linux descriptor path

open_points.subject: A18 transaction atomicity versus SQLite journal mode
open_points.text: “A call that fails writes and changes no record” conflicts with “in whatever journal mode the database file holds; the kernel sets none and checks none” because no condition excludes a journal mode that cannot provide that failure/crash guarantee
open_points.question: Is every SQLite journal mode accepted while the no-partial-record guarantee remains unconditional, or must incompatible modes be refused or replaced?
options: accept every mode and make the guarantee conditional
refuse modes that cannot preserve the guarantee
set a release-fixed safe journal mode
provide the guarantee outside SQLite journaling
open_points.default_guess: refuse incompatible modes while preserving an existing compatible mode

open_points.subject: A18 failed store call after encountering a symlink
open_points.text: The normative rule says a later link makes the call fail “writing no record (rule 3)”, rule 3 permits “a published file no record names”, but required test 4 says the call fails “with nothing written”
open_points.question: May a store call that encounters a symlink leave a complete unreferenced published file, or must it leave no filesystem write at all?
options: no record may be written but an unreferenced published file may remain
neither records nor files may be written
the stricter no-file rule applies only to the value-area scenario in required test 4
open_points.default_guess: neither records nor files may be written by a call that fails because it encountered a symlink

open_points.subject: A20 unsupported-host detection
open_points.text: A20 says “the kernel neither tests the host nor defines what it does on an unsupported one”, while A03 rule 8 requires the kernel to check that bubblewrap is present and that a probe execution succeeds before startup, thereby testing facilities used by the sandbox
open_points.question: Must startup detect missing Linux namespace and limit facilities through the required sandbox probe and refuse to start, or is behavior on such a host wholly undefined with no required test?
options: run the A03 probe and refuse startup when it fails
perform no facility test and leave all behavior undefined
probe only bubblewrap presence but not whether its required isolation facilities work
open_points.default_guess: run the A03 probe and refuse startup when the required sandbox facilities do not work
